title: Dashboard slimming and signal refactoring guidance
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a pragmatic playbook for identifying high-value signals, reducing metric cardinality, and refactoring dashboards to lower query cost and cognitive overhead while preserving actionable SRE/PM workflows. The focus is inference-serving telemetry (latency, token counts, KV cache hit rates, model fallbacks) but much of the guidance applies to feature-level instrumentation as well.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce dashboard query cost by ~40% in high-traffic panels within 3 months (pilot projects).
- Cut unique metric tag cardinality where possible (retain high-cardinality only when it supports operator actions).
- Maintain or improve time-to-detect for P0/P1 incidents (no regression on key SLO alerting).
- Clear ownership and migration plan for each retired/merged metric.

High-level principles:
1) Operator-first: Keep signals that directly map to an action (restart node, scale pool, revert rollout, throttle tenant). If a metric doesn’t suggest an operator action after 2 minutes of investigation, deprioritize it.
2) Cost-aware retention: Prioritize panels that are queried or used for oncall. For infrequently used deep-dive charts, use sampled or lower-resolution sources.
3) Surface vs deep: Dashboards should be layered — concise top-level cards for SLOs and business-impacting signals, and separate deep-dive workbooks for investigations.
4) Reduce duplication: If two metrics convey the same story, pick the one with clearer semantics and cheaper cardinality.
5) Guardrails for new signals: Require owner, expected cardinality, intended consumers, and a sunset plan for any new metric.

Discovery checklist (how to find what to slim):
- Inventory: Export all panels for a dashboard and group by underlying metric name and tag set.
- Query cost analysis: Identify top-10 most expensive dashboard queries (based on query planner or cost logs).
- Usage: Look at dashboard access logs for the last 90 days; mark rarely-viewed panels (<=1 view/month) as candidates.
- Alert alignment: Any metric that currently triggers an SLA/SLO alert must be reviewed with the oncall lead before change.
- Ownership check: Flag metrics without an explicit owner.

Metric classification rubric (keep, refactor, sample, retire):
- Keep: Metrics that are used by alerts, runbooks, or customer-facing reports; cardinality <= 100 per minute; low cost.
- Refactor: Metrics with useful semantics but costly cardinality (example: per-tenant per-model per-route latency). Refactor to aggregate-first semantics (per-route, then sample tenants).
- Sample: Metrics that are good for debugging but not required at full fidelity (trace samples, rare error logs). Collect at 1-5% and tag sampled=true.
- Retire: Metrics with no owner, low usage, and no link to runbooks or tickets for future use.

Concrete refactoring patterns:
- Aggregate-first counters: For per-request compute (e.g., per-tenant token_count), emit an aggregated counter at route-level and an optional sparse per-tenant histogram sampled at 0.5–2% to support tail analysis.
- Cardinality bucketing: Normalize freeform keys (e.g., model_variant -> map uncommon variants to "other" after top-k). Use mapping at instrumentation or ingestion shim.
- Label trimming: Remove high-cardinality labels used only for offline joins (replace with id that maps in a short-lived lookup).
- Synthetic keys for dashboards: Create dashboard-side derived keys for grouping (e.g., tenant_tier = free|paid|enterprise) and keep telemetry labels minimal.

Sampling and trace sparsity guidance:
- Trace sampling budget: Define a global default sampling of 0.5% for traces, with an adaptive fast-path that bumps sampling to 5–20% when tail latency SLO breaches or error-rate spikes.
- Session-aware sampling: If a session triggers a P1 error or fallback flow, retroactively mark prior spans for retention for that session.
- Anchor traces: When an oncall or evaluation requires deep correlation, use an indexed small-store (tenant->trace ids) so we can fetch associated traces without increasing global sampling.

Dashboard UX and composition rules:
- One-screen SLO center per service: top row = SLO health (error, p50/p95 latency), second row = cost signals (token_rate, tokens_per_request, avg_batch_size), third row = capacity/fallbacks (node_util, queue_latency, fallback_rate).
- Use sparse heatmaps for latency-by-tenant only in drilldowns — heatmaps are high-cardinality and expensive.
- Pin critical runbook links to panels (link to the runbook action list and incident playbook).
- Replace many small single-metric panels with multi-series compact panels that use small multiples instead of separate queries.

Operational migration plan (example):
Stage 0 — Discovery and owner alignment (2 weeks):
- Export dashboard metrics and cost; assign owners; open a lightweight RFC per dashboard.
Stage 1 — Pilot refactor (3 weeks):
- Choose 2 dashboards with highest query cost. Implement aggregate-first metrics and sampling on a canary subset of traffic (10% region).
- Measure query cost and operator time in oncall simulations.
Stage 2 — Broader rollout (4–6 weeks):
- Roll changes to all tenants; switch dashboards to new metrics and hide old ones. Keep old metrics retained for 30 days as a rollback safety.
Stage 3 — Sunset old metrics (after 30 days if no regression):
- Delete retired metrics and remove associated ingestion jobs. Close RFC and update catalog.

Example queries and implementation notes (pseudo-SQL / prometheus-ish):
- Aggregated token rate (cheap):
  sum by (route) (rate(tokens_processed_total[1m]))
- Sampled per-tenant tail latency (sparse):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tenant) (rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{sampled="true"}[5m])))
- Cardinality-reduced error count:
  sum by (route, error_class) (rate(error_count_total[5m]))
  // map error_class unknown values to 'other' at ingestion layer

Checklist for adding new metrics (enforced at PR):
- Owner listed in metric docs
- Estimated cardinality and expected cardinality with worst-case estimate
- Intended consumers (oncall, product analytics, offline analysis)
- Sunset date or retention period
- Resource estimate: expected downstream storage cost increase per month

Runbook and alert migration notes:
- Redirect alerts to new aggregated metrics where possible; keep a bridging alert on old metric for 30 days with reduced priority.
- Update SLO queries and explain changes in the SLO playbook.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should default trace sampling be for private deployments where privacy concerns differ? Suggest per-customer opt-in with outbound trace redaction.
- What retention tiering do we want for infra vs product metrics? We should store infra SLO metrics at higher fidelity for longer than experimental product signals.

Action items (next steps):
- Owners (Ravi, Lina) to run discovery export for top-15 expensive queries by 2025-03-10.
- Implement aggregate-first token_count shim for /generate route (PR: observability/pull/88) and test in canary region.
- SRE to run oncall drill using new dashboards on 2025-03-21 and report time-to-detect.

Appendix: helpful links and templates
- Migration RFC template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Metric+Migration+RFC
- Pilot tracking sheet (copy): /shared_drives/engineering/observability/pilot-tracking-sheet
- Sample ingestion transform (pseudocode):
  if model_variant not in TOP_K_VARIANTS: model_variant = 'other'

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive; please call out any critical panels you think cannot be aggregated or sampled. The goal is to reduce cost and noise while keeping operator effectiveness equal or better.
